0.long_answer: Peyronie's disease is characterized by fibrous plaque formation in the tunica albuginea of the penis. These fibrous plaques disrupt the normal elastic properties of the penile tissue, leading to curvature, pain, and difficulties in achieving or maintaining an erection with sufficient rigidity. As a result, many men with Peyronie's disease experience erectile dysfunction, which can also have psychological ramifications due to its impact on sexual function and overall quality of life.
